A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dynamic Group Attention study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark scores, inference latency, optimization and noise-robustness experiments, sparsity measurements and ablations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–7 and the experimental plots.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same token scoring, grouping, complementary tokens and decoding. Algorithm 2 replaces an intermediate mask permutation with direct selection of the same mask blocks; this simplifies its description without establishing a different attention computation.

E1.justification: SlimPajama, LongBench-E, WikiText2 and Proof-pile retain the same training or evaluation roles. The long-context tasks and sparsity scenarios are unchanged; video/audio applications remain prospective in both versions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain vanilla LLaMA2-7B, MInference, StreamingLLM and LM-Infinite as comparators. The vanilla-model comparisons and appendix ablation comparators are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain the same models, preprocessing, training budgets and evaluation settings, including 1,000 training steps, EM evaluation at 4K–32K and latency evaluation at 4K–16K.

E4.justification: The noise-robustness and optimization analyses, attention-sparsity visualizations, and Appendix F ablations of group size, focal-token selection, importance rate and complementary tokens are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same 100-example sparsity estimates and averaged noise-response measurements. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported experimental values and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, DGA retains a LongBench-E average of 21.14 in Table 1, average EM of 27.7 in Table 2 and 16K latency of 28.79 ms in Table 3.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces merely unequal group sets with explicitly disjoint sets. Equation (10) changes normalization to sum_g alpha_bar_g |G_g| = 1, and Equations (21) and (31) introduce sum_g m alpha_g = 1. These are local formal revisions; theorem conclusions and the remaining derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The supervised reformulation, sparsity analysis, group-coding benefits and DGA efficiency claims remain. Although the shortened conclusion omits its explicit robustness-and-efficiency phrase, those claims remain in the unchanged abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: The interpretations of sparsity, robustness, convergence and accuracy–latency tradeoffs are unchanged. Appendices G and I retain the same applicability discussion, qualifications and future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix D revises the mask-construction instructions to reference the original mask directly when constructing complementary and final masks, eliminating an intermediate rearranged mask. Hardware, hyperparameters, data-processing instructions and code-access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Adding PMLR to the existing Chen et al. reference for Core Context Aware Transformers is a bibliographic metadata update.

P1.justification: The conclusion is lightly condensed, the acknowledgments add CPSF postdoctoral funding, and publication metadata is updated. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–7 retain their displays and placement. Algorithm 2 is shortened from six numbered steps to five, reducing its displayed box, with limited text reflow around other edits.

improvement.justification: v4 improves local precision by explicitly requiring disjoint groups and making Algorithm 2 reference the original mask directly. The benefit is limited: normalization constraints are revised without reworking the surrounding derivations, while the empirical evidence and principal claims remain unchanged.
